def-abstract-oriented-knot-cobordism:
## Definition

An oriented circle is a smooth one-dimensional manifold diffeomorphic to the standard oriented circle. An abstract oriented cobordism from an oriented circle $C_0$ to an oriented circle $C_1$ is a compact oriented smooth surface $F$ together with orientation-preserving identifications of its incoming and outgoing boundary components such that $\partial F=-C_0\sqcup C_1$. Here $-C_0$ denotes the same circle with its orientation reversed. The cobordism is abstract: no embedding of $F$, $C_0$, or $C_1$ into a common three- or four-manifold is included in the data.
def-locally-flat-proper-surface-and-conc:
## Definition

Let $X$ be a four-dimensional manifold with boundary and let $W$ be a compact surface with boundary. An embedding $e:(W,\partial W)\to(X,\partial X)$ is proper when $e^{-1}(\partial X)=\partial W$. It is locally flat at an interior point of $W$ when there are neighborhoods of the point and its image and a homeomorphism of pairs from those neighborhoods to $(\mathbb R^4,\mathbb R^2)$, with the standard linear plane $\mathbb R^2\subset\mathbb R^4$. It is locally flat at a boundary point when there are such neighborhoods and a homeomorphism of pairs to $(\mathbb R^4_+,\mathbb R^2_+)$, where $\mathbb R^4_+=\{x_4\geq0\}$ and $\mathbb R^2_+=\{x_2=x_3=0,\ x_4\geq0\}$; the line $\partial\mathbb R^2_+$ lies in $\partial\mathbb R^4_+$. A collar of a boundary circle of $W$ is an embedding of that circle times $[0,\varepsilon)$ into $W$ that is the identity on the circle at parameter $0$; a concordance collar is required to agree with the corresponding product collar of the ambient end. A smooth proper surface has the analogous smooth charts and collars, which are also topological locally flat charts.
lem-rational-isotropic-subspace-saturate:
## Statement

Let $H$ be a free abelian group of rank $2g$ and let $V:H\times H\to\mathbb Z$ be a bilinear form. Write $H_{\mathbb Q}=H\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$ and extend $V$ $\mathbb Q$-bilinearly to $H_{\mathbb Q}$. If $L\subset H_{\mathbb Q}$ is a $\mathbb Q$-subspace of dimension $g$ and $V(x,y)=0$ for all $x,y\in L$, then $M=H\cap L$ is a rank-$g$ direct summand of $H$ and $V|_{M\times M}=0$.
thm-locally-flat-codimension-three-arc-u:
## Statement

Let $M=S^3\times[0,1]$. Let $\alpha:[0,1]\to M$ be a locally flat proper embedding with endpoints $(p,0)$ and $(p,1)$ and with product collars at those endpoints. Then there is a continuous family of homeomorphisms $H_t:M\to M$, $t\in[0,1]$, such that $H_0$ is the identity, every $H_t$ preserves the two boundary levels and is the identity near them, and $H_1(\alpha([0,1]))=\{p\}\times[0,1]$. If in addition $\alpha(s)=(p,s)$ on neighborhoods of $0$ and $1$, the family can be chosen so that $H_1(\alpha(s))=(p,s)$ for every $s$.
def-reverse-mirror-of-oriented-knot:
## Definition

Fix the orientation-reversing reflection $r:S^3\to S^3$ chosen for the mirror convention in the oriented connected-sum definition. If $K$ is a smooth oriented knot, its mirror $r(K)$ carries the orientation induced from $K$ by $r$. The reverse mirror of $K$, denoted $K^\dagger$, is the image $r(K)$ with its knot orientation reversed. Thus $K^\dagger$ changes both the ambient orientation convention and the orientation of the knot.
def-smooth-knot-concordance:
## Definition

Let $K_0,K_1$ be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented three-sphere $S^3$, and let $I=[0,1]$. A smooth concordance from $K_0$ to $K_1$ is the image of a smooth proper embedding $f:S^1\times I\to S^3\times I$ whose lower and upper boundary circles are $K_0\times\{0\}$ and $K_1\times\{1\}$. The embedding has product collars at both ends: in a neighborhood of each boundary circle it is the corresponding knot embedding crossed with the interval coordinate. Orient the annulus so that its boundary, with the boundary-orientation convention, is $-K_0\times\{0\}\sqcup K_1\times\{1\}$. The knots are smoothly concordant when such an annulus exists.
def-locally-flat-pl-knot-concordance:
## Definition

Use the standard PL three-sphere given by the boundary of a fixed PL four-simplex and the product PL structure on $S^3\times I$. A PL map is a map that is affine on every simplex after finite subdivisions of triangulated domain and target. An oriented PL knot is the image of a PL embedding of an oriented triangulated circle into this PL three-sphere. Two such knots are PL concordant when a PL embedding of a triangulated annulus into $S^3\times I$ has them as its lower and upper boundary circles with boundary orientation $-K_0\times\{0\}\sqcup K_1\times\{1\}$, and the embedding is proper, locally flat in the PL category, and has PL product collars at the two boundary circles. PL local-flatness means that each interior pair chart is PL-homeomorphic to $(\mathbb R^4,\mathbb R^2)$ and each boundary pair chart is PL-homeomorphic to $(\mathbb R^4_+,\mathbb R^2_+)$. Annuli with cone singularities or other non-locally-flat points are excluded. This definition makes no assertion identifying PL concordance with smooth or locally flat topological concordance.
def-locally-flat-topological-knot-concor:
## Definition

Let $K_0,K_1$ be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented three-sphere $S^3$, and let $I=[0,1]$. They are locally flat topologically concordant if there is a topological proper embedding $f:S^1\times I\to S^3\times I$ whose image is a locally flat annulus, whose boundary circles are $K_0\times\{0\}$ and $K_1\times\{1\}$, and whose annulus orientation induces the boundary $-K_0\times\{0\}\sqcup K_1\times\{1\}$. The annulus must have product collars at both ends. No differentiability of the annulus is assumed.
lem-general-knot-reverse-mirror-sum-is-r:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$, let $B^4=\{x\in\mathbb R^4:\lVert x\rVert^2\le1\}$ with boundary $S^3$. The oriented connected sum $K\#K^\dagger$ bounds a smooth properly embedded disk $D\subset B^4$ for which the squared radial function $\rho(x)=\lVert x\rVert^2$ restricts to a Morse function on the interior of $D$ with all critical points of index $0$ or $1$.
lem-smooth-slice-iff-concordant-to-unkno:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. A smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere bounds a smooth properly embedded disk in the unit four-ball $B^4=\{x\in\mathbb R^4:\lVert x\rVert^2\le1\}$ if and only if it is smoothly concordant to the standard unknot.
lem-smooth-and-topological-knot-concorda:
## Statement

On oriented ambient-isotopy classes of smooth knots in the standard three-sphere, smooth concordance is an equivalence relation, and locally flat topological concordance is an equivalence relation.
lem-knot-concordance-compatible-with-con:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. If $K_0$ and $K_1$ are concordant in the smooth category and $J_0$ and $J_1$ are concordant in the same category, then $K_0\#J_0$ and $K_1\#J_1$ are smoothly concordant. The same implication holds when both given concordances and the resulting concordance are required to be locally flat and topological.
lem-smooth-and-topological-slice-genus-m:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every smooth oriented knot $K$ in the standard oriented three-sphere, let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ be the set of genera $g(F)\in\mathbb N_0$ of connected compact orientable smooth properly embedded surfaces $F\subset B^4$ with oriented boundary $K$, and let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{top}}(K)$ be the corresponding set for locally flat topologically properly embedded surfaces. For each surface, $g(F)$ is the nonnegative integer determined by $\chi(F)=1-2g(F)$. Both sets are nonempty and have least elements.
thm-knot-concordance-is-an-abelian-group:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. The set of smooth oriented knot concordance classes in the standard three-sphere is an abelian group under connected sum, with identity the standard unknot and inverse of $[K]$ represented by the reverse mirror $K^\dagger$. Separately, the set of locally flat topological oriented knot concordance classes is an abelian group under connected sum, with the same identity and inverse convention.
def-smooth-and-topological-slice-genus:
## Definition

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere and let $B^4$ be the standard four-ball with boundary $S^3$. Let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ be the set of genera of connected compact orientable smooth properly embedded surfaces $F\subset B^4$ with oriented boundary $K$. Let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{top}}(K)$ be the set of genera of connected compact orientable locally flat topologically properly embedded surfaces $F\subset B^4$ with oriented boundary $K$. For each such surface, its genus $g(F)$ is the nonnegative integer determined by $\chi(F)=1-2g(F)$. Define the smooth slice genus and the locally flat topological slice genus by

$$
g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K):=\min\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sm}}(K),\qquad g_4^{\mathrm{top}}(K):=\min\mathcal S_{\mathrm{top}}(K).
$$
lem-linking-number-equals-four-dimension:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be disjoint finite rational $1$-cycles in the boundary $S^3$ of the standard oriented $4$-ball $B^4$, each represented as a finite rational linear combination of oriented knots. Let $P$ and $Q$ be finite rational $2$-chains in $B^4$ with $\partial P=\alpha$ and $\partial Q=\beta$, with common standard product collars at their respective boundaries and with their interiors in general position. Then the signed interior intersection number $P\cdot Q$ equals the bilinear extension of the linking number $\operatorname{lk}(\alpha,\beta)$ defined by positive meridians in $S^3$.
lem-locally-flat-slice-surface-bounds-se:
## Statement

Assume full AC. Let $D$ be a locally flat properly embedded disk in the standard four-ball $B^4$ with boundary an oriented knot $K\subset S^3$, and let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected oriented Seifert surface for $K$. After matching product collars and pushing the interior of $F$ slightly into $B^4$, the closed locally flat surface $\Sigma=F\cup_KD$ bounds a compact connected oriented locally flat three-manifold $R\subset B^4$. The conclusion includes an oriented ambient product neighborhood of $R$ on both sides, with the positive normal push-off along the $F$ portion of $\partial R=\Sigma$ lying on the complementary side of $R$.
def-metabolic-seifert-form-and-algebraic:
## Definition

Assume the full Axiom of Choice when a knot's Seifert pairing is formed. An integral Seifert lattice is a pair $(H,V)$ in which $H$ is a free abelian group of rank $2g$ for some $g\geq0$, and $V:H\times H\to\mathbb Z$ is bilinear with $V-V^T$ unimodular. The rank-zero lattice is allowed, with the determinant of its empty skew matrix equal to $1$. A metabolizer is a primitive direct summand $M\subset H$ of rank $g$ such that $V(x,y)=0$ for every $x,y\in M$; the lattice is metabolic when it has a metabolizer. A chosen Seifert surface of an oriented knot gives such a lattice through the positive-push pairing. Its form is algebraically slice when that lattice is metabolic.

An isomorphism of integral Seifert lattices $(H,V)$ and $(H',V')$ is an integral group isomorphism $P:H\to H'$ satisfying $V'(Px,Py)=V(x,y)$ for all $x,y\in H$. Let $\mathcal S$ be the commutative monoid of these isomorphism classes under orthogonal direct sum, where $(H,V)\oplus(H',V')$ has underlying group $H\oplus H'$ and pairing $V\oplus V'$, with the rank-zero lattice as identity. The integral algebraic concordance group $G_{\mathbb Z}$ is the abelian group generated by symbols $[V]$ for $[V]\in\mathcal S$, subject to $[V\oplus W]=[V]+[W]$ and $[M]=0$ for every metabolic lattice $M$. Two selected Seifert forms are algebraically concordant when they represent the same element of $G_{\mathbb Z}$. This form relation does not assert the existence of a smooth or locally flat topological concordance annulus between the knots.
lem-slice-disk-induces-seifert-metaboliz:
## Statement

Assume full AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the oriented standard $3$-sphere, let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected compact smooth oriented Seifert surface of genus $g$, and let $D\subset B^4$ be a locally flat properly embedded disk with oriented boundary $K$. Then the positive-push Seifert lattice $(H_1(F;\mathbb Z),V)$ is metabolic: it has a rank-$g$ primitive direct summand on which $V$ vanishes identically.
